title: kv-cache: improve memory management and eviction heuristics to reduce fragmentation/paging/spillover
author: Marcus Chen
description: Motivation: production workloads with long-context chat and multi-tenant KV usage were triggering frequent host paging and OOMs under memory pressure due to small fragmented allocations and suboptimal eviction priority. This change implements a set of coordinated improvements to reduce fragmentation, avoid unnecessary GPU-to-host spillover, and make eviction decisions workload-aware. High-level changes: 1) Introduced a defragmentation pass that coalesces small free segments during low-load windows and before large allocations. 2) Implemented a size-class aware allocator for KV shards to reduce internal fragmentation. 3) Added an eviction scoring function that weighs recency, access frequency, and estimated downstream compute cost to avoid evicting hot KV entries that are cheap to recompute. 4) Implemented a paging throttle that delays non-critical spillover to host when GPU memory is transiently constrained and allows prioritized allocations for low-latency requests. 5) Added metrics and tracing for per-shard fragmentation, eviction score distribution, spill events, and time-to-restore after eviction. 6) Exposed knobs for aggressive defrag, paging throttle thresholds, and eviction bias at runtime via the serving config. Tests and benchmarks: microbenchmarks show a median reduce in host spill events by 72 percent on mixed chat embeddings workloads and 35 percent lower tail latency for 95th percentile requests under contention. End-to-end canary in perf-canary reduced observed OOM incidents on medium-size hosts from 6/day to 0/day across a 48-hour window. Rollout plan: start with canary on internal perf-cluster, enable defrag in conservative mode for 24h, then enable full heuristics for 7 days with continuous monitoring. If regressions are detected, auto-fallback to prior eviction policy is available. Compatibility and migration: default behavior follows prior policy unless operators opt into the new heuristics by setting config key kv.eviction.policy=v2. No storage or data migration required. Implementation notes: defrag runs as a background job bounded by a CPU and memory budget; it uses retired segments and avoids pausing inference by migrating only when live usage allows. The allocation library changes are localized to runtime/kv_allocator.{cc,h}. Eviction scoring is implemented in runtime/kv_eviction.cc with unit tests. Metrics are added to telemetry/kv_metrics.{cc,h} and surfaced in the Console dashboard under KV Cache -> Memory. Security and safety: no new permissions or external calls introduced. Performance tuning: added a default conservative set of thresholds derived from cluster telemetry; teams can tune per-pool. Related work: continues the work from prior PRs focused on spillover and defrag heuristics (see refs ENG-4010 and PRs around kv-cache-eviction-spillover).

review_comments: Ayesha Khan: This looks good overall, but can we get more details on the defrag migration strategy? Is there any case where migration could increase tail latency? Marcus Chen: Defrag is designed to be opportunistic and bounded. It only migrates segments when target alloc can be satisfied and will yield if live access patterns change. We added instrumentation to abort a migration if it would impact p95. We also added a conservative default to run defrag only when the system sees sustained low CPU usage.

Liam O'Neill: The eviction scoring introduces compute-cost estimates; how are those computed and kept up-to-date? Marcus Chen: We use a light-weight estimator based on model type, average sequence length and historical restore time sampled by telemetry. It's bounded to a max estimate and decays over time. Teams can opt-out per-pool. Added comments and tests to validate estimator behavior.

Sofia Patel: Any risks for multi-tenant fairness with the new paging throttle? Marcus Chen: Paging throttle uses tenant-priority signals from the scheduler to prioritize allocations for high-priority routes. Default is equalizing to maintain fairness; ops can adjust with kv.paging.priority_bias.

Ayesha Khan: CI showed a flaky integration test earlier, did we root cause? Marcus Chen: Flake was due to race in test harness; fixed by adding a synchronization barrier. The CI job failed once and passed on rerun; detail in CI logs.

release_notes: Improved KV cache memory management with defragmentation to reduce internal fragmentation and OOMs.
New eviction scoring that balances recency, frequency, and recompute cost to avoid evicting busy but cheap-to-recompute entries.
Paging throttle to reduce unnecessary GPU->host spillover and improve tail latency under bursty load.
New metrics for fragmentation, eviction score distribution, and spill events exposed in Console.
Runtime knobs to tune defrag aggressiveness and eviction bias; default is conservative and opt-in via kv.eviction.policy=v2.
